note: Shared merge conformance vectors. Identical file in bopa and notable. For every vector both suites assert merge(a,b)==expected, merge(b,a)==expected, merge(expected,a)==expected and merge(expected,b)==expected. See docs/couch-sync-protocol.md.

vectors.name: page-disjoint-strokes
vectors.why: Both devices drew offline on the same page; union keeps everything, ordered by stroke createdAt.

vectors.name: page-erase-beats-draw
vectors.why: One device still holds a stroke the other erased. The tombstone wins on both devices.

vectors.name: page-both-erase-different-strokes
vectors.why: Tombstone sets union; each device's erase applies to the other's surviving copy.

vectors.name: page-tombstone-keeps-earliest-deletedAt
vectors.why: Both devices erased the same stroke; a deletion cannot un-happen, so the earliest observation stands.

vectors.name: page-fractional-seconds-not-string-compared
vectors.why: REGRESSION: '…33.871Z' sorts BEFORE '…33Z' lexicographically but is later in time. A string compare would pick the wrong winner and silently drop the newer background.

vectors.name: page-scalar-tiebreak-by-device-id
vectors.why: Identical updatedAt: the tiebreak is updatedBy by UTF-8 order, so 'ipad' beats 'boox' on both devices.

vectors.name: page-createdAt-merges-to-minimum
vectors.why: The page was created before one device learned about it; the earliest creation time is the true one.

vectors.name: page-images-union-and-tombstone
vectors.why: Images follow the same add/remove rules as strokes.

vectors.name: page-rename-lww
vectors.why: A page named on one device keeps that name on the other: the later write wins. An unnamed page is null, not an empty string, so 'never named' stays distinct from 'named empty'.

vectors.name: page-rename-cleared-lww
vectors.why: Clearing a page's name is an edit like any other, so the later write wins even though its value is null — a name removed on one device does not come back from the other.

vectors.name: page-identical-inputs
vectors.why: The common case after a settled sync: merging a document with itself changes nothing.

vectors.name: page-sheet-survives-undeclaring-peer
vectors.why: A page's sheet says how the ink already on it is laid out, so a writer that has not learned the field cannot un-declare it by writing last: the winner's value is used only when it has one. Otherwise one sync from an older build would reflow every page it touched.

vectors.name: page-two-sheets-later-write-wins
vectors.why: When both sides declare a sheet — which in practice means the size was changed, since it is fixed at creation — it resolves like any other scalar: the later write.

vectors.name: notebook-pageids-ordered-union
vectors.why: Winner's page order is authoritative; pages only the loser knows are appended in the loser's relative order.

vectors.name: notebook-page-delete-beats-page-add
vectors.why: A page deleted on one device must not be resurrected by the other device still listing it.

vectors.name: notebook-rename-and-move-lww
vectors.why: Scalar metadata is last-writer-wins as a whole record, so title and folder never split across devices.

vectors.name: notebook-default-sheet-survives-undeclaring-peer
vectors.why: Same rule as a page's own sheet, for the size new pages in the notebook are created with.

vectors.name: notebook-trash-travels
vectors.why: The Trash is a state of the notebook, not of one device: the later write is a trashing, so the notebook leaves the library on both.

vectors.name: notebook-restore-beats-earlier-trash
vectors.why: Restoring is an ordinary later write, so it wins the scalar envelope and clears deletedAt. Merging deletedAt as a tombstone-style earliest-wins union instead would make a restore impossible to express: the peer still holding the trashed copy would re-bury it.

vectors.name: notebook-later-edit-outlives-trash
vectors.why: deletedAt travels in the scalar envelope (§5.5), so an edit written after the trashing carries deletedAt=null with it and the notebook returns to the library — the same rule §6.4 applies to a real deletion, and the same known consequence.

vectors.name: folder-rename-lww
vectors.why: Folders carry nothing that can conflict internally.

vectors.name: folder-trash-travels
vectors.why: A trashed folder hides its whole subtree from this one field, so the subtree is hidden on both devices without either touching a descendant.

vectors.name: notebook-bookmark-unstar-beats-earlier-star
vectors.why: Bookmarks are last-writer-wins per page: the later un-starring wins over the earlier star, and is kept as a removed entry so it reaches a peer that still holds the star.

vectors.name: notebook-bookmark-restar-beats-earlier-unstar
vectors.why: The property a tombstone union could not express: a page keeps its id, so starring it again after un-starring must win. Remove-wins would make the second star unreachable forever.

vectors.name: notebook-bookmarks-union-sorted-by-page
vectors.why: Two devices starred different pages offline; both survive, and the result is sorted by pageId so the encoded document is byte-stable whichever device wrote it.

vectors.name: notebook-bookmark-dropped-with-its-page
vectors.why: A star on a page that has since been deleted is dropped rather than kept: it can no longer be navigated to, so keeping it would show a line that does nothing when tapped.

vectors.name: notebook-outline-order-from-winner
vectors.why: Outline order follows the same ordered add-wins rule as pageIds: the winner's order is authoritative and entries only the loser knows are appended in the loser's relative order.

vectors.name: notebook-outline-rename-lww
vectors.why: Entry content is last-writer-wins per entry id, independently of where the entry sits in the order.

vectors.name: notebook-outline-removal-travels
vectors.why: A deleted entry stays in the list as a removed tombstone. Dropping it here would let the peer that still holds it put the entry straight back on the next merge.

vectors.name: notebook-outline-depth-clamped-on-decode
vectors.why: A depth from a build that allows more levels degrades to the deepest this one understands instead of failing to merge, and both implementations must clamp identically or the two would render different outlines.

vectors.name: notebook-outline-entry-survives-its-pages-deletion
vectors.why: Unlike a bookmark, an outline entry whose page was deleted is kept by the merge. An entry is keyed by its own id but would be tested on pageId, and dropping it loses the record that stops the peer re-adding it on the next merge — so readers skip dangling entries instead, and deleting a page marks its entries removed as an ordinary edit.

vectors.name: split-one-page-per-sheet
vectors.why: Writing past the sheet made the page taller; each sheet becomes a page, in order.

vectors.name: split-page-within-its-sheet-is-untouched
vectors.why: A page that fits its sheet must not be divided, or every open would file a page.

vectors.name: split-stroke-crossing-the-boundary-stays-whole
vectors.why: Ink belongs to the sheet it starts on and is never cut; counting sheets from where content starts is also what makes a second run a no-op.

vectors.name: split-overhang-alone-makes-no-second-page
vectors.why: Sheets are counted from where content begins, not how far it reaches — measuring the extent would file an empty page on every open, for ever.

vectors.name: split-image-below-the-sheet-travels-with-it
vectors.why: Images are placed by their top edge, by the same rule as ink.
